Great music really brings a certain mood and feel to a game that otherwise would be lost, World of Warcraft is definitely my favourite for music in an MMO game, some of it just incredible.

Stepping in to the bustling Alliance capital of Stormwind or the Horde capital of Orgrimmar, even just the Log-in screen all had a completely different and epic feel to it with the different music.

I played too much WoW when it first came out, all that music still rings in my head, especially the launcher. I think that this piece is the lynch pin for future songs, I have heard it refereed to as the main theme already and I can see that it is essentially a repeating set of...I don't know what you call them, notes, stanzas, cords? What ever it is it repeats in different styles representing the different elements of the game: discovery, travel, combat, victory, and loss.

I'm hoping we see some of the WoW music in the new Warcraft film, it's definitely iconic as far as the series goes and it would be pretty cool for those that have played before.

When someone says "excuse me" or "pardon me" do you ever reply? Let's say this happens after a belch or sneeze, is it common manner to say "you're excused" or do you pretend you didn't hear?

Depends. Most times I just ignore them, or say "bless you" if someone sneezes.

I did, however, after a series of unfortunate events turned a bad day into an even shittier one, answer back with a loud "No" when someone said "pardon me" after belching in my ear on a packed rush hour train.

The guy looked shocked at my reaction, and so was I. It wasn't like it was his fault. There wasn't exactly room to manoeuvre.
But if you just ignore it, is it considered rude?

Gassy Lady: Excuse me, did you not just hear my sudden and audible flatulence. Isn't someone going to pardon me?!

Average UK'er: Na, you're alright love.

No. Ignoring it is the polite response when someone passes gas then excuses themselves. Acknowledging it is the rude response.

For sneezes. its polite to say bless you before they say anything.
